### When files stop being enough

If one agent on one machine is all you have, a markdown file is a fine place to start. Files stop being enough at three moments.

- Several agents need the same memory. A file sits in one folder on one machine. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code to the same VAAS-X account and each can recall from the same memory. Whether an agent reaches for it without being asked depends on the agent.

- A fact changes mid-project. A file keeps the old line next to the new one. In VAAS-X you mark the old note as superseded, so recall stops ranking it highly.

- You need what worked, not just what matches. A file gives back lines that look similar. VAAS-X records how each episode turned out and ranks recall toward what worked.

You do not have to take our word for the results: every benchmark has a reproduction guide you can run yourself. VAAS-X is not a chatbot and it is not a place to keep files.

### What “memory that survives a power cycle” looks like

One device, one memory store, three moments. Nothing the device recorded is lost when the power goes.

#### 1. Running

The device records what it saw, what it did and how it turned out. Each of those is one episode.

#### 2. Power off

Power is cut or the device resets. The device’s memory store is not touched.

#### 3. Power on

The device asks what worked in a similar situation and gets the stored episodes back, best outcomes first.

## How It Works

No integration project. No specialist hardware. Memory starts from the first datapoint.

### Step 1 â Connect

Point a data source at VAAS-X: a JSON address, an RSS or Atom feed, a CSV or JSON file, an MQTT topic or a WebSocket. Numbers become sensor channels, and text and ids are kept with their values so an agent can read them back. No schema design or configuration.

### Step 2 â Accumulate

Every operational event is stored as a memory episode â what was observed, what happened, and what the outcome was. Memory builds continuously from the moment you connect.

### Step 3 â Recall

When something happens, VAAS-X finds the closest matching episodes from history in milliseconds â on a standard CPU, and with no cloud call in on-device deployments.

### Step 4 â Rank by outcome

Because every episode records its outcome, recall ranks what actually worked above what only looked similar. Your agent or application records the outcomes and uses what comes back; VAAS-X does not change a model’s weights.

### This is not a chatbot. This is not a vector database. This is operational memory infrastructure.

VAAS-X doesn't generate responses. It keeps a record of what your systems saw, what they did and how it turned out, and brings back the closest past cases when they are needed â persistently, privately, and without ongoing AI compute costs.
